question: The City & Guilds 2382 18th Edition exam is:
option_b: Open book, 60 questions, 2 hours
correct_text: Open book, 60 questions, 2 hours
explanation: It's open book — your copy of BS 7671 plus a calculator — 60 questions, 2 hours.

question: What is the typical minimum pass mark, and the score you should really be aiming for?
explanation: Pass marks can vary slightly by cohort — treat 60% as the floor and aim well above it.

question: Because the exam is open-book, your revision time is best spent:
option_a: Memorising every table value word for word
option_b: Learning the structure of the book and practising finding the right clause/table quickly
correct_text: Learning the structure of the book and practising finding the right clause/table quickly
explanation: The real skill tested is fast, accurate navigation and application — not rote recall.

question: If a question gives you numerical data, the safest approach is:
option_a: Guess based on similar past questions
option_b: Work the calculation through methodically using the correct formula and reference
option_d: Skip and never return to it
correct_text: Work the calculation through methodically using the correct formula and reference

question: Which item is essential to bring to the exam alongside ID?
option_b: The current edition of BS 7671 and a scientific calculator
option_c: A copy of the On-Site Guide only
correct_text: The current edition of BS 7671 and a scientific calculator
explanation: Check your exam centre's exact permitted-materials list beforehand — some restrict which additional guides are allowed.

question: "Basic protection" refers to protection against electric shock:
option_b: Under normal, fault-free conditions
correct_text: Under normal, fault-free conditions
explanation: Fault protection is the single-fault-condition case (ADS, earthing, bonding).

question: What does "Zs" represent?
option_a: The impedance of the earth electrode only
option_b: The total earth fault loop impedance (external + internal)
option_d: The resistance of the line conductor only
correct_text: The total earth fault loop impedance (external + internal)
explanation: Zs = Ze + (R1 + R2).

question: PME stands for:
option_b: Portable Mains Equipment
correct_text: Protective Multiple Earthing
explanation: PME describes a TN-C-S supply where the combined PEN conductor is earthed at multiple points by the DNO.

question: In a TT earthing system, the installation's means of earthing is provided by:
option_b: A PEN conductor from the DNO
option_d: Bonding to gas and water pipes only
correct_text: A local earth electrode

question: SELV is defined as:
option_a: A system not exceeding 50V a.c., electrically separated from earth and other systems
option_b: Any circuit protected by an RCD
option_c: A circuit with a functional earth connection
correct_text: A system not exceeding 50V a.c., electrically separated from earth and other systems

question: "Prospective fault current" (PFC) is:
option_a: The current that would flow for a fault of negligible impedance
option_b: The maximum current a cable can carry continuously
option_c: The rated current of the protective device
option_d: The design current of the circuit
correct_text: The current that would flow for a fault of negligible impedance

question: A "competent person" under BS 7671 is someone who:
option_a: Holds a City & Guilds 2382 certificate only
option_b: Has the skill, knowledge and experience to avoid danger to themselves and others
option_d: Has more than 10 years' experience regardless of training
correct_text: Has the skill, knowledge and experience to avoid danger to themselves and others

question: The term "exposed-conductive-part" describes:
option_a: A touchable conductive part, not normally live, that can become live under fault conditions
option_b: Any conductive part of the installation, live or not
option_c: A live conductor with damaged insulation
correct_text: A touchable conductive part, not normally live, that can become live under fault conditions

question: An "extraneous-conductive-part" is:
option_b: A conductive part liable to introduce a potential, not forming part of the electrical installation (e.g. structural steel)
correct_text: A conductive part liable to introduce a potential, not forming part of the electrical installation (e.g. structural steel)

question: What is a "circuit protective conductor" (cpc)?
option_a: The conductor connecting exposed-conductive-parts to the main earthing terminal
option_b: The line conductor of a final circuit
option_c: A conductor used only for functional earthing
correct_text: The conductor connecting exposed-conductive-parts to the main earthing terminal

question: RCBO is an abbreviation for:
option_a: A device combining overcurrent and residual current protection in one unit
option_b: Ring Circuit Breaker Outlet
correct_text: A device combining overcurrent and residual current protection in one unit

question: "Diversity" in an electrical installation refers to:
option_a: The requirement to use different cable types on every circuit
option_b: The allowance made because not all connected loads run simultaneously at full demand
correct_text: The allowance made because not all connected loads run simultaneously at full demand

question: Part 3 (Assessment of General Characteristics) requires the designer to consider all of the following EXCEPT:
option_a: Purpose, supplies and structure of the installation
option_b: External influences (ambient temperature, water, etc.)
option_d: The exact make and model of every light fitting
correct_text: The exact make and model of every light fitting

question: "External influences", coded AA/AB/AC..., relate to:
option_a: The financial cost of the installation
option_b: Environmental conditions affecting equipment selection (temperature, altitude, water, impact)
correct_text: Environmental conditions affecting equipment selection (temperature, altitude, water, impact)

question: Before working on an existing installation, BS 7671 requires assessment of:
option_b: Supply/installation characteristics likely to affect the design, including maximum demand, earthing arrangement, and condition of equipment to be reused
option_d: The colour of existing cables only
correct_text: Supply/installation characteristics likely to affect the design, including maximum demand, earthing arrangement, and condition of equipment to be reused

question: Maximum demand of an installation is assessed:
option_a: By adding the rated current of every appliance with no allowance
option_b: Taking diversity into account, using recognised guidance
option_d: It is not required under Part 3
correct_text: Taking diversity into account, using recognised guidance

question: Compatibility (Part 3) requires checking that:
option_a: All equipment is the same colour

option_d: All circuits use the same device rating
correct_text: Equipment characteristics (starting current, harmonics, leakage) won't harmfully affect other equipment or the supply

question: Which is an example of "AD" (presence of water) external-influence classification?
option_b: AC2 – altitude
correct_text: AD4 – splashing

question: For a TN system, the maximum disconnection time for a final circuit ≤32A is:

correct_text: 5s

question: Fault protection (single-fault-condition shock protection) is most commonly achieved by:

correct_text: Automatic Disconnection of Supply (ADS)

correct_text: A single circuit from an isolating source, live parts not connected to earth or another circuit

question: SELV and PELV are protective measures classed under:

option_d: Obstacles and placing out of reach

question: The nominal voltage limit for SELV/PELV under normal conditions is:

option_b: Only permitted where supervised/controlled by skilled or instructed persons
correct_text: Only permitted where supervised/controlled by skilled or instructed persons

option_a: Be removable with a standard tool for maintenance
option_b: Only be removable by destruction, solvents or heat — not by hand
option_c: Be any colour so long as present
correct_text: Only be removable by destruction, solvents or heat — not by hand

question: A barrier providing basic protection must give at least a degree of protection of:

correct_text: IPXXB (IP2X), or IPXXD on accessible horizontal top surfaces where required

question: Which is correct about RCDs and TT systems?

option_d: TT systems don't require an earth electrode
correct_text: Because Ze is often too high for overcurrent devices alone, an RCD is almost always essential for fault protection

question: To confirm automatic disconnection will occur in time on a TN system, you must check:
option_b: That Zs does not exceed the tabulated maximum for that device and disconnection time
correct_text: That Zs does not exceed the tabulated maximum for that device and disconnection time

correct_text: Detect arc faults that conventional overcurrent/RCD protection may miss, reducing fire risk

question: Under Regulation 421.1.7, AFDDs are required as a minimum for certain final circuits ≤32A in premises such as:

correct_text: HMOs and similarly higher-risk residential premises listed in BS 7671

question: Where fitted, an AFDD should be installed:
option_a: At the furthest point of the circuit from the origin
option_b: At the origin of the final circuit it protects
option_d: In the socket outlet itself only

question: Regulation 422 deals with:
option_a: Precautions for locations with particular risks — fire, explosion, escape routes, high fire load
option_b: Voltage drop only
correct_text: Precautions for locations with particular risks — fire, explosion, escape routes, high fire load
